name: Template: policy, research and meta
summary: TEMPLATE: what the charity does, the causal chain to the outcome, the year modelled, the bottom line in years of healthy life per $1,000 (quote it live in the write-up), and the biggest uncertainty. If the result is more than ten times its cause's median on the site, say why ("more than ten times its peers because …").

source.title: charityevals' estimate: policy, research and meta

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Programmes with no outcome data
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for a programme that publishes no outcome data at all: it is valued at the result per dollar of the same kind of work elsewhere on the site, read live, and counts less by the shared slider "How much we count a programme we could only estimate from similar ones" (docs/normalization.md 2.12). A programme with some outcome data is modelled from it in the chain above, with wide ranges, never here.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Spending on the modelled program(s) in the year modelled
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: program expenses, in US dollars, for the activities modelled below and the same year as the reach numbers (say the year in the label and the summary). Cite the audited statement of functional expenses (or the annual report) and the page. Other currencies: a row in local currency times @fx.usd_per_<cur>_<year> (the IRS yearly average, else the World Bank's; add the fact with scripts/link-fx.py), never a typed rate.

rows.label: Total expenses (all programs, management, fundraising)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: total expenses for the same year, from the same document.

rows.label: Program expenses (all programs)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: program-service expenses for the same year, from the same document.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ program expenses)
rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programs in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do.

rows.label: Cost of the modelled program, including overhead
People or animals per year the policy or research would affect
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the population under the law or rule, or that the research's results reach, per year. 0 with an explanation if the charity only moves money.

rows.label: Value per unit affected per year, in units of value

source.title: TEMPLATE: charityevals model of the downstream intervention

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the downstream benefit per person or animal per year, in units of value, built from the same shared figures a direct model of that benefit would use (deaths at @moral_weights × $life_value_multiplier, the site's SADs per change). Where it is the result per dollar of a program the site models, read that model live (#model-id) instead of typing its number.

rows.label: Probability the change happens because of this work
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the probability that the policy passes or the research changes decisions in the period, given the charity's work. Base it on a reference class (share of similar bills passed, of similar campaigns won) and say which. A not-yet-proven meta organisation's chance of success is @meta.success_chance_new_org, not this row.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (Your values → How impact is counted; docs/normalization.md 2.9). Never the charity's or an evaluator's own years.

rows.label: Years from the win until the policy takes effect
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the wait from the win to when the rule or law applies (its own implementation date, cited); discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the policy takes effect
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit.

rows.label: Discounted years of impact
Expected value of the policy or research (before adjustments)
Money moved or raised for other charities in the year modelled (US$)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: donations the charity moved or raised for other charities in the same year as the cost, gross, from its own report (0 with an explanation if it moves none). Valued only through the shared rows below: never a multiple of cash, a counterfactual share or a leverage ratio of the charity's or an evaluator's own.

rows.label: Money moved per dollar of the charity's cost
rows.explainer: Context, and the donors' share of the resources with credit by share of resources on.

rows.label: Value of a dollar to global health and poverty charities (GiveWell's Top Charities, live), units of value
rows.explainer: GiveWell's four Top Charities (Against Malaria Foundation, Malaria Consortium's seasonal malaria chemoprevention, Helen Keller Intl's vitamin A, New Incentives), each at its result on this site under your values, weighted by what GiveWell directed to each in 2024 (50%, 29%, 18%, 4%).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: This organisation moves money only to global health and poverty charities, so a dollar moved is valued at that destination alone (GiveWell's Top Charities, live).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: 1× GiveDirectly), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment. Shifted money was going to be given anyway; it is credited only for the gain. Where it would have gone is valued at GiveDirectly's live result (GiveWell's model), as Ambitious Impact does, times a shared multiple (1×, from 0 to 3×).

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity: about half the money moved wouldn't otherwise have been given (Ambitious Impact's Effective Giving Incubation report), from 35% to 80%.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone.

rows.label: Value of the money moved (units of value)
Careers changed to high-impact work in the year modelled
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: people the charity moved into high-impact jobs in the year modelled, from its own survey (0 with an explanation for most charities).

rows.label: Pay a career changer gives up per year (US$)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: what they could earn elsewhere less what they take, per year.

rows.label: Years a career changer stays in high-impact work
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: from the charity's follow-up survey or a labelled reference class.

rows.label: Years a career changer stays, discounted
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Value of a dollar of the new employers' work (units of value)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the employer's live result per dollar (#model-id) where the jobs are at one charity the site models; the moved-money destinations where they are spread over many.

rows.label: Share of the career changes the charity caused
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the changes that wouldn't have happened without the charity, from its own survey of what people would have done, or a labelled reference class.

rows.label: Value of one career change (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one career-change step (docs/normalization.md 2.8).

rows.label: Value of the career changes (units of value)
Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how far the effect size above should be trusted for this charity's setting: publication bias, self-report bias, replication, differences between study populations and this program. A multiplier (1 = take the studies at face value), the product of its parts; say each part, its anchor (the same adjustment in another model of this intervention) and the range.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the outcome that would not have happened without the program (other providers, existing trends, government). Cite coverage data or trend data where possible.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: where other organisations contributed to the same outcome (co-funders, coalition campaigns, government delivery), this charity's share of everyone's spending on it. Others' in-kind work counts too: government staff time, partners' own delivery costs, and volunteers' unpaid time (beyond any stipend the charity pays, which is in its cost), valued at the local wage for the hours given. 1 when it delivers alone.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Total value (units of value)
rows.explainer: The adjustments apply to the policy and research branch; money moved counts its counterfactual through the shared new-money share, career changes through their own share.

rows.label: Value per dollar
rows.explainer: For WELLBYs, rename the uov_* rows to wellbys_* and report in wellby. For animals, rename them to sads_* and add the species section of the corporate-campaign template (output ced_per_donor_dollar). For climate, start from the climate skeleton.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared default for this kind of work (@staff_pay.share_research_policy; facts/staff_pay.json has one per kind: goods, staff-delivered, research and policy, advocacy, media). Where the charity's financials give salaries and benefits, use them instead: an estimate input (salaries ÷ total expenses, Form 990 Part IX lines 5–9) with its source.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared pay gap for this kind of work (@staff_pay.gap_research_policy); pick the fact that fits the staff (local delivery, health and field, research and policy, advocacy, media, UK charity). Don't type a gap in.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff (in-kind donation)
How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: This model's cost per outcome is the charity's past spending over what it won (estimate_basis past_average), so the next dollar is valued at the shared share of the average (docs/normalization.md 2.10). 1 in `published`: what the past average itself says.

rows.label: Share of the full cost paid by cash donations
Units of value per dollar you give
rows.explainer: The modelled programmes' result for their share of the spending, plus the programmes with no outcome data (the proxy section).

rows.label: Spending on programmes with no outcome data at all, in the year modelled
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: programme spending, same year and accounts as program_spend, on the charity's programmes that publish no outcome data whatsoever (no reach, no results, nothing to build the chain on); not part of program_spend. 0, with that reason, when every programme has some outcome data: partial data keeps the chain above with wide ranges.

rows.label: Result per dollar of comparable programmes on the site (units of value per dollar you give)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the same kind of work elsewhere on the site, read live: median(#model-a, #model-b, #model-c) of this family's or intervention's models, or the one nearest evaluated programme (#model-id) where there are fewer than three; name them and why they are comparable. Never a typed number, never a peer from another kind of work. (#givedirectly is only the skeleton's placeholder.)

rows.label: Share of the programme spending here that has no outcome data
rows.explainer: The modelled programmes' result counts for the rest of the spending.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar you give, from programmes with no outcome data
rows.explainer: Comparable programmes' result for this share of the spending, counted less by the shared slider: missing data is always discounted, the same way in every model.

output.label: Units of value per dollar you give
